subject: POC evaluation plan & runbook — next steps and owners
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>

Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: POC evaluation plan & runbook — next steps and owners

Hi Emma,

Thanks again for the call today — great to meet you and Carlos. Quick recap and a proposal to keep momentum:

- Goal we heard: validate 1) 2x improvement in throughput for anonymized clinical notes search latency, and 2) <150ms per-token generation under your 512-token median sequences.
- Success criteria (draft): see attached success_criteria_sheet.xlsx — a mix of latency percentiles, throughput targets, and qualitative accuracy thresholds on the sample prompt set you shared.
- Proposed trial cadence: 2-week technical trial (environment setup + synthetic runs), followed by a 2-week validation with your real anonymized dataset. Total 4 weeks.
- Ownership: Redwood will handle model serving, config, and instrumentation. Verdant to provide access to a 2-week anonymized dataset and a point person for acceptance testing.

I've attached a short runbook (poc_runbook_v0.2.pdf) that enumerates tasks, owners, and a simple test script we can run together. Can you confirm the acceptance owner on your side and whether the suggested 4-week cadence works? If so, we’ll schedule a kickoff slot and send environment access instructions.

Next steps I propose now:
1) You confirm owners and datasets by EOD Wednesday (Dec 2).
2) We schedule a 45-minute kickoff next week to walk the runbook and get infra credentials.
3) Redwood will provision a dedicated trial environment scoped to the dataset size you shared.

Thanks — looking forward to moving this along.

Best,
Ben Carter
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwoodinference.com
+1 (415) 555-0124

Hi Ben — thanks for the clear recap. Quick answers:

- Acceptance owner: Carlos Jimenez (Sr. Manager, Data Platform). He will be the primary sign-off for the validation stage.
- Dataset: We can generate a 2-week anonymized extract from our clinical notes pipeline; security redaction team needs the runbook to confirm the process but should be straightforward.
- Cadence: 4-week timeline looks reasonable. We’d prefer the technical trial to run the week of Dec 7 so our infra team can do prep this week.

I’ll loop in Carlos on the kickoff scheduling. Please add any items in the runbook you think our security team will ask for and we’ll expedite review.

Thanks,

Great — thanks Emma. Carlos, welcome. I pushed an updated runbook (v0.2) with a small security appendix (expected artifacts: IAM roles, minimal S3 view-only bucket, TLS/endpoint expectations). Rishi will own the infra provisioning and initial model tuning; Marissa will coordinate the acceptance tests and eval scripts.

Key timeline (proposed):
- Dec 6: Redwood prepares trial environment (credentials + test harness).
- Dec 7–10: Technical trial (synthetic + small subset of your anonymized data).
- Dec 13–17: Validation runs and acceptance testing (Carlos & team).
- Dec 20: Sign-off meeting and next steps (production readiness discussion).

Carlos — can you confirm your team can provide the anonymized extract by Dec 6 and a point contact for security review? If anything on the timeline looks tight, tell us and we’ll adjust.

Ben
